factsAccepted: EBITDA margin declined 200 bps from 10.0% (FY2024) to 8.0% (FY2025), with EBITDA falling from $204M to $168M (-$36M) even though revenue grew from $2,040M to $2,100M (+2.9%). Margin contracted while volume rose, indicating a profitability-per-dollar problem rather than a demand problem. Applying the FY2024 margin to FY2025 revenue would have implied ~$210M EBITDA, versus $168M actual, a ~$42M margin drag.

Approximately 70% of revenue ($1,470M) is firm-fixed-price (FFP) multi-year contracts without economic price adjustment (EPA) clauses; only ~30% ($630M) is cost-plus or carries escalation. On the FFP book, input-cost inflation cannot be passed through to the customer, so all material and labor inflation on that revenue compresses margin directly. The ~30% cost-reimbursable/escalating book recovers most cost increases, concentrating the entire inflation impact on the FFP portfolio.

Materials cost rose to $735M (35% of revenue) up +12% YoY like-for-like, and direct labor rose to $546M (26% of revenue) up +8% YoY. The increases are input-price driven (commodity and wage inflation), not efficiency-driven: there is no disclosed deterioration in productivity, scrap, rework, or throughput. The cost increase is being absorbed because contract prices on the FFP book are fixed, not because operations became less efficient.

Backlog stands at $5.6B (2.7x annual revenue) with book-to-bill of 1.1, indicating strong, growing demand and a deep book of future-period work. The company is not losing orders or market share; on the contrary, it continues to win work. This rules out a demand-shortfall or market-decline explanation and indicates the locked backlog itself carries the embedded pricing exposure: future periods will recognize revenue at pre-inflation fixed prices on the FFP portion of backlog.

Estimating the inflation impact attributable to the FFP book: of the $735M materials cost, ~70% ($514.5M) supports FFP revenue; the embedded +12% inflation on that base is ~$61.7M. Of the $546M labor, ~70% ($382.2M) supports FFP revenue; the embedded +8% inflation is ~$30.6M. Combined, ~$92M of input inflation is attributable to the no-EPA FFP book and is structurally unrecoverable through pricing. Net realized EBITDA drag (~$42M) is smaller than gross inflation because the ~30% cost-plus/escalating book recovers its share and revenue growth provides partial absorption, but the unrecovered FFP inflation is the dominant driver of the 200 bps compression.
factsNeedingClarification: Contract-by-contract EPA clause language and exact pass-through eligibility (proprietary contract terms not in public filings)
Program-level (contract-level) gross margin and the specific FFP contracts that are underwater (public filings aggregate by segment)
Strength of REA / claims position per contract (requires legal review of change-order history, government-caused delay, and constructive change facts)
Forward input-cost hedging positions and supplier contract terms for materials (not publicly disclosed)
Internal labor productivity and overhead absorption detail by program (not disclosed)
